Th e goals of nutritional therapy for GSD I are to prevent hypo-
glycemia, correct metabolic derangement, and provide optimal
nutrition to support growth and development. Carbohydrates
from complex sources should provide about 60% to 70% of the 
total caloric intake. A portion of the carbohydrate may be pro-
vided by the uncooked cornstarch. Protein should come from
lean sources, providing 10% to 15% of total kcal. Fat should pro-
vide less than 30% of total kcal, and dietary saturated fat should 
be limited. Two-thirds of the kcal will be given during daytime 
feedings to allow for carbohydrates to be distributed frequently 
and evenly over the 24-hour period. One-third of kcal are
administered overnight, primarily from a carbohydrate source
via cornstarch or tube feedings. Meals high in starch, without
